items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: I did a record date I'm proud of called 'Teddy Wilson's All Starts' ... when he was on trumpet, and had Vic Dickinson on trombone and Bob Wilber on reeds.

ctx.x: That's right. He's very happy these days.

Yeah, I work quite often with him at jazz festivals. Of course, recently up there in Colorado Springs, Gibson's party. And I did a record date I'm proud of called "Teddy Wilson's All Starts" for the Chiaroscuro label a couple years ago when he was on trumpet, and had Vic Dickinson on trombone and Bob Wilber on reeds. Bob, incidentally, did the little sketch arrangements this time. And Major Haley on bass and we had Oliver Jackson on drums. And we tried to do kind of like we did in the old days. We made three…

items.title: Bob Wilber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: He loved Teddy Wilson’s piano. He’d bought some of the albums. And he took the whole family, I guess it was around 1942, to Cafe Society to hear Teddy Wilson’s band.

ctx.x: Did your parents encourage you to have a safety net?

Yeah. Well my father came from a small town in Ohio and he went to college and went on to get a Master’s degree and came to New York and went into textbook publishing, and he was very successful at it. And of course being in that field he knew all the © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

professors in all the universities, and he really would have liked me to have gone to one of the ivy league schools. So I guess when I was about 16 we began to go around and we were going around to the colleges and he’d introduce me to the various professors and everything. By the age of 16 I was hooked on jazz, and I said this is very nice, Dad, and Princeton is lovely, the campus and everything. But I said this doesn’t feel right for me. So he said, “Okay, well look, we’ll go up to Eastman School in Rochester.”…
